answer: Because the ivory fee is applied at the river exit, the crystal audit totals the burn and the ledger publishes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 10% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
